newsitem.title: UK: Ofgas enquiry into UK gas market rigging nears end.
newsitem.headline: Ofgas enquiry into UK gas market rigging nears end.

text.p: A official from UK natural gas industry regulator Ofgas said on Tuesday that he expects an investigation into potential UK spot market manipulation to be finished by the end of this month.
Kyran Hanks, Ofgas head of transport pricing, told a conference on Tuesday that Ofgas is now investigating the spot market, following a number of complaints that the market may have been rigged.

Hanks added that not all in the market believe Ofgas has any role in the spot market. "One company said 'why are you even investigating something which doesn't concern you'", he said. "But if prices go up because one large company is abusing its position, then it's clearly a matter for the regulator," he added.

The investigation was triggered by a steep rise in spot gas prices towards the end of last year. Asked if there was a link between rising prices and the decision by British Gas plc to turn down production at its Morecambe field off the UK's west coast, Hanks replied: "It has been suggested to us that the two are linked. Any suggestions made have to be considered, so we're considering it".

He said that Ofgas has no view on whether the price rise is due to manipulation until the investigation is complete, and he admitted that the regulator's options may in any case be limited if manipulation is proved.
"If we find the the price rise is due to the abuse of a dominant position, we could just publish a report to say so", he said. "As to something more interventionist, I don't know what we could do".

Ofgas has so far carried out fifteen or twenty interviews with major players as part of its investigation. It expects to finish by the end of this month, after which it will be another two or three months before it publishes the report.
